## Grids and geometry: tests and checks {#sec-ch15-ch03-tests}

This catalogue accompanies @sec-ch03. The source pin is `snapy@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0`. No snapy
executable, installed snapy package, CUDA test or multi-rank test was run for this draft; "registered" below
describes source evidence, not a measured pass.

### Independent report checks

The command `python3 src/snapy_report/ch03/geometry_check.py` checks the closed forms of @sec-ch03 with numpy and
sympy, without importing snapy. Its committed output is `src/snapy_report/ch03/geometry_check.out`; the pytest
wrapper `src/tests/test_checks.py` runs it with every other chapter's checks.

| output label | assertion | tolerance | what it does not establish |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[C1]`-`[C3]` | radial face centroids, moment and shift; the test rationals | exact symbolic | the compiled helpers |
| `[C4]`-`[C5]` | spherical-polar averages, centroid, face-pressure and angular-momentum identities | exact symbolic | the code's area factor (@sec-ch03-sphpolar) |
| `[C6]`-`[C9]` | gnomonic angle, solid angle, lower/raise, uniform-pressure flux | $10^{-8}$ to $10^{-15}$ | the velocity source terms |
| `[C10]` | Morton order of a $4\times4$ block grid | exact | 3-D order, cubed-sphere corners |
| `[C11]` | cross-panel slide below $n_g-\tfrac12$ | exact bound | the exchange itself |

: Independent checks of @sec-ch03 and their limits. {#tbl-ch15-ch03-independent}

: Registered tests that @sec-ch03 relies on. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch15-ch03-registered}

The three rows marked "main after chengcli/snapy#303" describe main at chengcli/snapy `9ad0936779ae001dba65c9eafccaa7c058686c97`, while the rest of this table is pinned at `e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0`. Their status is the one the body of chengcli/snapy#303 states: CPU `ctest -j1` 114 of 115 on the branch (the body does not name the commit of that run, so it is not shown to include every row marked here), the one failure `test_straka` (no `pd-combine` on that machine) [source: chengcli/snapy#303 body; sha: snapy@546b1afd80d47a437a92ead745ef525f8335094a (PR head); deck/run: CPU `ctest -j1`, the commit of the branch and the deck not stated in the body]. With the radial-exact switch on, the split column of `radial_exact_split_gap` drifted from one block by $8.0\times10^{-7}$, $6.3\times10^{-8}$ and $2.3\times10^{-9}$ at $n_1$ = 32, 64, 128 before the seam took the centred slope, and by 0 after; the new seam tests fail on the parent source [source: chengcli/snapy#303 body; sha: snapy@546b1afd80d47a437a92ead745ef525f8335094a (PR head); deck/run: the column of `radial_exact_split_gap` at nz 32/64/128, device not stated in the body]. On CUDA (RTX 5090) the switch-on arm gave exactly 0 at all three resolutions, and the switch-off arm met a round-off gap of $1.9\times10^{-14}$ at $n_1=128$, which failed the exact-zero assertion it then had; snapy@84512197b4516c242719ec2b1da425206991802b bounded it by $10^{-13}$ [source: chengcli/snapy#303 body; sha: snapy@f5c0cff427db4681d0e65e40ae5a88c974e1a617; deck/run: CUDA `ctest -j1` on an RTX 5090]. With the covariance on, the six-panel seam test had two-valued dry-mass seam faces 288/576 (as the body gives them) and a scalar and mass drift of $5.03\times10^{-10}$ before the cross-panel exchange carried the $x_1$ ghost rows, and 0 faces and $2.40\times10^{-15}$ after; the new arm fails with that change reverted ($5.03\times10^{-10}$ against $10^{-13}$) and passes at the head ($2.4\times10^{-15}$) [source: chengcli/snapy#303 body; sha: snapy@546b1afd80d47a437a92ead745ef525f8335094a (PR head); deck/run: `test_flux_positivity_cubedsphere_flux_covariance_python`, device not stated in the body].

### Gaps

No test checks the spherical-polar $m_2$ and $m_3$ curvature sources, the synthesised $x_2$-$x_3$ ghost corners, the
face-state suffix rule on its own, the `cylindrical` type, or `DeviceTest.interpolate_LR` and
`GnomonicEquiangle.area_vol`, which print and assert nothing.
